text:
Maria C: Heads up — I'm kicking off a short cross-team sync to define the signal contract and dashboard scope for KV + prefix cache effectiveness. Need runtime, infra, and console inputs so we can ship useful panels and low-noise alerts. Context: hit rate, evictions, and reuse-by-workload are the primary signals we want to track.

Jay K: +1. Can you list the exact metrics you want emitted from the runtime vs what infra should derive/aggregate? Also needs privacy constraints for tenant labels. :eyes:

Maria C: Proposed emitter surface (from runtime):
- kv_cache_hit_total (labels: model, tenant_hash, prefix_bucket, workload)
- kv_cache_miss_total (same labels)
- kv_cache_eviction_total (reason, model, tenant_hash, prefix_bucket)
- kv_cache_seen_prefixes_total (model, tenant_hash, prefix_bucket)
- kv_cache_prefix_reuse_total (model, tenant_hash, prefix_bucket, reuse_window)

Note: 'tenant_hash' should be a 4-char deterministic hash (low cardinality) to preserve privacy. 'prefix_bucket' is a coarse-bucketed prefix length or a hashed-prefix-bin to avoid raw prefix leakage. We'll derive hit_rate and reuse_pct in the telemetry pipeline / dashboards.

Ashok P: Runtime overhead concerns — emitting all these counters per request could be noisy. Suggest sampling 1% and also emitting aggregated per-request counters every minute. We can implement per-worker local counters and flush every 1m to reduce cardinality & cost.

Maria C: Good — sampling + local flush sounds right. We should have two emission modes: full (for Dedicated/Private opt-in) and sampled (default for Hosted). Put the mode as a metric label emission_mode=sampled|full.

Li Wei: For Console dashboards, I suggest these panels:
- Global hit-rate (5m rolling): sum(kv_cache_hit_total)/sum(kv_cache_hit_total+kv_cache_miss_total) by (model)
- Tenanted hit-rate heatmap: same as above by tenant_hash (top N buckets)
- Evictions rate (1m): increase in kv_cache_eviction_total by reason
- Reuse by workload: kv_cache_prefix_reuse_total / kv_cache_seen_prefixes_total by workload type
- Latency impact panel: left of token-latency p95 for cache hit vs miss - need correlation link from runtime traces

Sarah O: UX: we need these panels linkable from rollout pages and model routing policy screens. Also add a cost panel that estimates tokens saved = estimated_saved_tokens = (hit_rate * avg_tokens_saved_per_hit * qps) * cost_per_token; that's useful in the Optimize workstream.

Jay K: Ownership question: who maintains the pipeline that computes hit_rate? infra team? Or do we compute in Console via queries? Computing in the telemetry pipeline (OTEL/Prom -> metrics builder) reduces duplicated queries. But it needs to be consistent across environments.

Ashok P: I vote telemetry pipeline (infra) computes hit_rate and reuse_pct as derived metrics with configurable windows (1m, 5m, 1h). Console will then surface precomputed time series and avoid re-aggregation.

Maria C: Agreed. Infra to own derived metrics; runtime emits raw counters and a small set of pre-aggregates for Dedicated customers if they opt in. Also infra should publish the exact PromQLs and canonical metric names.

Li Wei: Cardinality guardrails: tenant_hash + model + prefix_bucket + workload is fine but we must cap distinct prefix_bucket cardinality to <= 200. If more unique buckets appear, trigger a sampling fallback. Add a metric kv_cache_prefix_bucket_cardinality to monitor this.

Jay K: Alerts: propose firing when hit_rate drops by >10% relative to 3d baseline for a model or when eviction rate spikes 3x. These should be P2 (investigate), not page unless it's at global scale. Thoughts?

Sarah O: Yes on alerting. Console rollout UX should show recent change in hit_rate alongside rollout steps to help correlate. Also add a small explainer tooltip about what 'reuse by workload' means.

Ashok P: Implementation notes for runtime: here's a quick sketch for local flush counters to avoid per-request emits:
```
// pseudo
struct LocalKVCounters {
  map[key] uint64 hits;
  map[key] uint64 misses;
  map[key] uint64 evictions;
}
on_request(prefix, tenant, model, workload) {
  key = slot(prefix_bucket(prefix), tenant_hash(tenant), model, workload)
  if (cache.hit) counters.hits[key]++ else counters.misses[key]++
}
periodic_flush() {
  emit counters to metrics backend; counters.clear()
}
```
Keep the key-space sharded by worker to avoid lock contention.

Maria C: Sounds good. Ashok, can you estimate runtime cost (cpu/memory) for default sampling + 1m flush? If >2% overhead we need different approach.

Ashok P: I'll bench and post numbers by EOD.

Li Wei: Console mocks — I'll put a draft dashboard with the panels above in https://redwood.internal/dashboards/cache-effectiveness-draft and share link when ready.

Maria C: Next steps/action items:
- Ashok: implement counters + sampling prototype + perf numbers (ETA EOD)
- Infra (Jay): define derived metric builder for hit_rate/reuse_pct and publish canonical PromQLs + aggregation windows
- Console (Li): mock dashboard and add rollout link targets + tooltip copy
- Product (Sarah): define alert thresholds and cost formula to show in panel

runtime-bot: PR created -> https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4212 (contains local counters + sampling flags).

Jay K: I'll schedule a 30m sync tomorrow to sign off on metric names and alerting. 

Maria C: Thanks all — please drop any open concerns here. If you want to change any metric name, do it in the next 24h before infra publishes the schema. :thumbsup:

Li Wei: quick q — should we surface 'reuse_window' buckets (e.g., 0-1s,1-10s,10-60s,>60s) or just a single sliding-window reuse_pct? I prefer buckets for histograms in Console. :thinking_face:

Ashok P: Buckets are helpful but increase label cardinality. Maybe make them optional emitted only in 'full' mode.

Maria C: Agreed. Let's go with optional buckets for Dedicated/Private and single reuse_pct for Hosted.

Sarah O: One more ask: provide a short readme for SRE/oncall about interpreting these signals (what to check first). I'll draft it once panels are up.

Maria C: Great — closing loop. Will post the canonical metric names + mapping doc when infra publishes. Thanks everyone! :pray:
